## Discovery & Translational Science

- **Hybrid proteogenomic metric improves risk stratification in titin cardiomyopathy** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.11.02.25338804)
  - Integrating long-read RNA sequencing (PSI-DCM-LR-15) with mass spectrometry-based peptide intensity (QPI) yielded a novel proteogenomic metric, QPI-PSI, for titin-truncating variant (TTN-TV) carriers.
  - QPI-PSI significantly outperformed traditional transcript-only metrics in predicting TTN-TV penetrance (AUROC 0.694 vs. 0.674, p = 0.002) and advanced heart failure expressivity (AUROC 0.639 vs. 0.600, p = 0.019 across 308 patients).
  - Predictive gains were particularly pronounced in women (AUROC 0.675 vs. 0.412, p = 0.028).

- **Clonally expanded B cells drive disease progression and cardiac fibrosis in Chagas cardiomyopathy** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.28.26366745)
  - Peripheral blood transcriptomics identified B cell clonal expansion signatures preceding late-stage disease progression in chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy (CCC).
  - Spatial transcriptomics and immunofluorescence confirmed dense populations of clonally expanded B cells co-localizing specifically with cardiac fibrosis in CCC hearts, which were absent in non-Chagas dilated cardiomyopathy.

- **Plasma renin activity stratifies cardiovascular risk and MRA benefit in hypertension** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.05.11.26352940)
  - A multicenter cohort of 16,600 hypertensive adults demonstrated a U-shaped association between baseline plasma renin activity and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), with nadir risk at 1.17 ng/mL/h.
  - Time-dependent Cox modeling showed mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA) therapy reduced MACE risk in patients with very low (<0.3 ng/mL/h; HR 0.59) and low (0.3–1.0 ng/mL/h; HR 0.71) renin levels, but conferred no benefit in high-renin patients (>3.0 ng/mL/h; HR 1.07).

- **Abdominal subcutaneous fat strongly correlates with cardiometabolic risk in young South Asian adults** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.02.01.26345312)
  - Longitudinal MRI tracking in the Pune Maternal Nutrition Study cohort (n = 590) demonstrated that abdominal subcutaneous adipose tissue (ASAT) at age 18 had substantially stronger associations with adverse lipids, glycemic control, blood pressure, and inflammatory markers than visceral fat (ASAT β = 0.45–0.88 vs. VAT β = 0.13–0.18).
  - Risk associations persisted through age 24 independently of total body mass index and birth weight.

- **[Biotech]** **CRISPR Therapeutics advances CTX213 toward clinical testing in type 1 diabetes** [X / @JessieChimni](https://x.com/JessieChimni/status/2124139635378913401)
  - Preclinical data support the therapeutic rationale for CTX213, an undisclosed gene-edited cell candidate, moving toward IND-enabling studies for type 1 diabetes.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

- **[Biotech]** **Intellia Therapeutics reports 36-month Phase 1/2 data for NTLA-2001 in ATTR-PN** [X / @GeneInvesting](https://x.com/GeneInvesting/status/2124139635378913401)
  - Long-term 36-month follow-up for the in vivo CRISPR gene-editing candidate NTLA-2001 demonstrated sustained, modest improvements in neuropathy impairment scores in transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy.

- **[Biotech]** **CG Oncology reports cretostimogene cuts recurrence risk in non-muscle invasive bladder cancer** [X / @adamfeuerstein](https://x.com/adamfeuerstein/status/2124139635378913401)
  - Clinical trial readouts for cretostimogene grenadenorepvec showed a 68% reduction in recurrence risk among patients with intermediate-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer.

- **[Biotech]** **Lexeo Therapeutics releases positive interim Phase 1/2 data for LX2020** [X / @BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2124139635378913401)
  - Interim clinical data for LX2020, an AAV-based gene therapy for PKP2-associated arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, demonstrated favorable preliminary cardiac signals.

- **[Biotech]** **Henlius registers Phase 1 trial for PD-1/IL-2 fusion protein HLX105** [X / @chuminhua432](https://x.com/chuminhua432/status/2124139635378913401)
  - Henlius initiated a first-in-human Phase 1 study evaluating HLX105, a bispecific PD-1/IL-2 fusion immunotherapy, in patients with advanced solid tumors.

- **[Biotech]** **Immutep reports Phase 2 eftilagimod alpha data in soft tissue sarcoma** [X / @jfais20](https://x.com/jfais20/status/2124139635378913401)
  - Phase 2 results for soluble LAG-3 protein eftilagimod alpha (efti) in soft tissue sarcoma support plans for a registrational study, pending external development funding.

- **[Biotech]** **Viking Therapeutics sees positive weight loss trends in VANQUISH trial site reports** [X / @bioinvestor24](https://x.com/bioinvestor24/status/2124139635378913401)
  - Unconfirmed clinical site reports from the Phase 2 VANQUISH study of dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist VK2735 suggest substantial weight loss efficacy in treated cohorts.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

- **[Big Pharma]** **Merck discontinues three Phase 3 trials of nemtabrutinib in blood cancers** [X / @WallStSai](https://x.com/WallStSai/status/2124139635378913401)
  - Merck has halted three Phase 3 clinical studies evaluating non-covalent BTK inhibitor nemtabrutinib across hematologic oncology indications.
  - The discontinuations mark a major strategic pipeline pullback for Merck's targeted hematology portfolio.

## Regulatory & Approvals

- **[Biotech]** **FDA turns back Capricor's deramiocel cell therapy citing data integrity violations** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/capricor-fda-duchenne-cell-therapy-deramiocel/875384/)
  - The FDA issued a Complete Response Letter rejecting Capricor Therapeutics' cardiosphere-derived cell therapy deramiocel for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
  - The agency took the unusual step of publicly citing serious data integrity violations that compromised trial findings, marking the drug's second regulatory rejection (noted by [@MartinShkreli on X](https://x.com/MartinShkreli/status/2124139635378913401)).

- **[Biotech]** **Summit Therapeutics FDA rejection letter reveals unstated regulatory concerns** [X / @NedPagliarulo](https://x.com/NedPagliarulo/status/2124139635378913401)
  - The published FDA rejection letter for ivonescimab revealed broader design and safety concerns than previously detailed in the company's public communications.

- **FDA publishes FY 2027 GDUFA III fee schedule and mandates electronic payments** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/industry/fda-user-fee-programs/generic-drug-user-fee-amendments)
  - The FDA finalized fiscal year 2027 Generic Drug User Fee Amendments (GDUFA III) rates, establishing ANDA application fees at $375,684 and Drug Master File fees at $109,899.
  - Effective October 1, 2025, the agency will strictly mandate electronic payment methods (eCheck, wire transfer, credit card) and discontinue paper-based payment processing.

**Worth watching:** Capricor's regulatory collapse over data integrity allegations may trigger broader FDA clinical quality control inspections across cell therapy sponsors.
